title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
author: Aayush Marasini, Barsat Khadka, Nick Rahimi
description: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. summary: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent.
takeaways: We introduce WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs of increasing capability on 42 WSP tasks across five tracks: reading, fixing and writing weights, recognizing edits that are impossible, and data-free compression.

Experimental benchmark results show that frontier agents can already read small networks and write working control policies without ever running them, but cannot yet patch language models, compress them without data, or tell an impossible edit from a hard one.
The networks whose weights the LLMs read and edit range from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models.
